synopsis: Accident Analysis & Prevention connects historical mining accident evidence, on-road driver behavior research, and simulation tools across the corpus. Ruff’s 2006 paper reported an average of five blind-area fatalities annually at US surface mines and quarries during 1999–2003, accounting for 12% of all fatalities; dump trucks represented 58% of equipment involved in blind-area fatal accidents [f3064, f3065, f3066]. Markkula et al.’s 2016 naturalistic rear-end emergency study found that braking responses depend on situational kinematics, arguing against a single fixed reaction time [f3495]. Road-truck FCW studies summarized in 2023 linked an 18% false alarm rate to underuse, with drivers ignoring warnings (12%) or stopping system use (11%); these findings concern on-road trucks rather than mining machines [f3332, f3333]. MineSim, published in April 2025, provides an open-source, peer-reviewed, scenario-based simulation test system and benchmark specifically for autonomous trucks in open-pit mines [f464, f15805].

relations.note: Both describe MineSim’s April 2025 publication and simulation role; the glossary also calls it a benchmark.
